item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is the preferable patch because its retry handling fails safely on seek errors and its tests more directly exercise the reported os.File/RetryAllMethods scenario. Neither patch is merge-ready: both violate the explicit requirement that Upload delegate to FilesService.Add.","reasons":["B tests Upload retry using content from os.Open with RetryAllMethods enabled, matching the reported workflow and streamed-content requirement more directly.","B makes failed seek/restore operations explicit errors. A silently returns after seek failures; because seeking to the end may already have changed the reader position, A can send an empty or partial body rather than merely disabling retries as its comment claims.","B avoids A's extra seekableBody type and keeps the narrowly used replay setup local and relatively easy to review.","Both correctly use internal/multipartbody.NewFile, validate required inputs, preserve Add's signature, and produce a buffered multipart body."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, response decoding, and error behavior instead of routing through Add, directly violating the frozen contract.","The seek helper's silent error paths may leave the underlying reader at a changed offset and then continue the request with corrupted body semantics.","The Upload retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than combining retry coverage with an opened-file source, and retry timing is not made deterministic in the added tests as it is in B's tests successfully exercised by the recorded gates implied contextually? Actually don't mention gates. Neither candidate adds the required source-reader failure test."],"risks_b":["Upload also duplicates Add rather than calling it, so future Add behavior can drift and the central reuse requirement is unmet.","It changes RawClient.Do semantics globally for failing io.ReadSeeker implementations and changes ownership/closing behavior beyond FilesService, though this is documented.","Validation combines empty filename and nil content into one generic error, which is less precise than A's parameter-specific errors; the required source-reader failure test is also missing."]}
